summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with fever, hematuria, and flank pain, consistent with pyelonephritis in the setting of a chronic indwelling Foley catheter and recurrent UTIs. He was treated with IV ceftriaxone initially, then transitioned to oral cefpodoxime as his white blood cell count normalized and symptoms improved. Bladder spasms were managed with Detrol after intolerance to oxybutynin. Catheter leakage persisted despite size and taping adjustments, necessitating urology follow-up. Hyperkalemia was addressed by reducing losartan from 50mg to 25mg daily, with normalization of potassium levels. Normocytic anemia was noted but deemed stable for outpatient follow-up. Chronic pain and polysubstance use were managed with continued home medications as documented. He was discharged home in stable condition with plans for follow-up in urology and primary care.
